The scalar barrier for Phi implies eventual positive lower bound for x when C>r, hence O(1/T) mean-vector correction for each positive trajectory. At C<r the per-capita rate tends to C-r. This is an analytic all-trajectory argument, not just a symbolic script.

originality.rationale: PASS: Boros-Hofbauer Theorem 14 for precisely the normalized four-species equations proves unique positive equilibrium for C>r, bifurcation and coexistence of an attracting equilibrium and two limit cycles, plus permanence. The 22-page arXiv full text was inspected at Eq. (8), Theorem 14 and its proof; it does not determine exact trajectory-independent concentration time means, a bounded finite-time endpoint correction, or the critical full inverse-time and logarithmic cumulative-production laws. The new coboundary identity and threshold asymptotic analysis are additional, not contained in equilibrium/cycle statements. General dynamic ACR results are about pointwise robustness and differ.

No pointwise supercritical convergence to the equilibrium is claimed because coexistence cycles can occur.

value.rationale: V PASS: This naturally motivated chemical oscillator has coexistence of stable/unstable cycles and equilibria, so their full observable concentration barycenter being identical is not a trivial equilibrium calculation. The O(1/T) endpoint terms identify quantitative mean invariants across basins; the critical universal t^-1 profile and logarithmic cumulative-production centering describe the natural chemical total-mass bifurcation sharply. No paper-sized general theory is required for this specific motivated dynamical theorem.

final_claim: For the specified four-species mass-conserving Wilhelm-Heinrich oscillator, all positive supercritical solutions have exactly determined equilibrium concentration means up to O(1/T), and at/below threshold all trajectories have sharp critical inverse-time or exponential extinction laws.
limitations: O(T^-1) error depends on positive initial data and parameters; no supercritical pointwise convergence asserted.
Critical C=r statement requires positive initial conditions.
